minutes.headline: Select Board adopted a single tax rate with no exemptions, and committed ARPA funds to small local requests.
minutes.summary: The board held the FY2025 tax classification hearing. It heard the assessors' recommendation, took public comment, and voted for a single rate with no exemptions. It also approved a T-ball field agreement, a skate park grant support letter, an Agricultural Commission appointment, an ARPA reallocation and small ARPA grants, and a purchasing card policy. The interim town manager's report covered projects, recruitment and health insurance, and the board discussed cannabis host agreements and the special town meeting debrief.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to adopt a single tax rate and not adopt any available exemptions, following the assessors' recommendation.
After a public hearing with comment for and against a split rate, the board held no further delay; one speaker had asked for a one-week hold.
The board voted to change the Marshall Park ARPA allocation to the remaining amount, then committed ARPA funds to Boys and Girls Club equipment, Historical Society items and fencing.
The board approved t-ball use of the old primary school property, a skate park grant support letter, an Agricultural Commission appointment, and a purchasing card policy.
The interim town manager reported a two-year property insurance renewal and said health insurance renewals are expected in mid-January with a high trend rate.

why_it_matters: The single-rate vote means residential and commercial property are taxed at the same rate in the FY2025 tax bills, so no shift of the levy onto commercial property is built into the average single-family bill.
The ARPA votes reallocate a fixed, one-time pool of federal money, so each dollar committed to a small request is no longer available for other projects.
Health insurance is a large, recurring cost in the town budget, and a high renewal trend would press on the FY2026 budget the board will be asked to set.
watch_next: Health insurance renewal figures, expected in mid-January.
The skate park support letter, due back at the next meeting with a December 31 grant deadline; the climate survey policy and goal-setting are postponed to December.
